question: In a centre code system using locality-sensitive hashing (LSH), if the similarity threshold is 0.8 and hash family has 20 functions, how many hash functions should be used for optimal performance?
solution:
The correct answer is __**16**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH)** is used to group similar items into the same buckets with high probability.
 
• The number of hash functions chosen is generally proportional to the similarity threshold.
 
• Formula commonly used:

 **Number of hash functions = Similarity Threshold × Total Hash Functions**
 
• Given:
 
 
• Similarity threshold = **0.8**
 
• Total hash functions = **20**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Step-by-Step Calculation:**

 
 
• Required hash functions

 = 0.8 × 20
 
• = **16**
 
 
 
• **Conclusion:**
 
 
• The optimal number of hash functions used = **16**.
 
 
 
• **About LSH:**
 
 
• LSH improves similarity search efficiency in large datasets.
 
• Higher similarity threshold requires more matching hash functions.
 
• Widely used in recommendation systems, plagiarism detection, and nearest-neighbor search.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• Similarity threshold determines matching strictness.
 
• More hash functions improve accuracy but increase computation.
